responsibility: This is the main executable implementation file of GCC’s MIPS backend, complementing mips.h and mips.md. It owns the target’s C/C++ logic for MIPS code generation across RTL expansion, addressing and symbol handling, calling convention and argument passing, prologue/epilogue and frame layout, constant and section selection, builtin expansion, vector and scalar mode support, scheduling helpers, assembler output, and many other target decisions, and it binds that behavior into GCC by defining the large set of TARGET_* hooks in the final targetm initializer.
same_name_distinction: Within the mips same-name group, this is the executable backend implementation file: it defines the MIPS target’s C logic and binds it into GCC through the TARGET_* hook initializer, whereas mips.h provides shared target declarations/macros, mips.md encodes RTL instruction patterns and attributes, and mips.opt declares command-line target options.
